chunks: Ali ibn al-Husayn, from Sa'd ibn Abdillah, from al-Hasan ibn Musa al-Khashshab, from Ghiyath ibn Kallob ibn Fays al-Bajali, from Ishaq ibn 'Ammar, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

Indeed, the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) performed the funeral prayer over a corpse. When he finished, a group of people came and said, 'O Messenger of Allah, the prayer over it was missed by us.' He (peace be upon him and his family) said, 'Indeed, the funeral is not prayed over twice; supplicate for it and say good things.'

Muhammad ibn al-Hasan said: This report is to be understood as indicating a type of dislike (karahah), for we have clarified the action of the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) with Sahl ibn Hunayf, and that he prayed over him (peace be upon him) five times. Whenever he finished from the five takbirs, a group of people would come, so he repeated it a second time for five times. And confirming that is what he narrated.

key_terms.الْكَرَاهِيَة: Dislike (a legal ruling less severe than prohibition)

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to pray the funeral prayer over the same corpse more than once?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* records the Prophet’s (peace be upon him) practice of repeating funeral prayers for latecomers, which Shia jurists interpret as *karahat tanzih* (recommended dislike) rather than *haram* (strict prohibition). This nuance is reinforced by Imam Ali’s (peace be upon him) precedent of praying five times over Sahl ibn Hunayf, demonstrating that multiple prayers are valid and meritorious for a single deceased person.
